title.narrative: Power to You(th) Uganda

description.narrative: The Power to You(th) Consortium believes that change starts within the community. We believein the power of young people, especially adolescent girls and young women (AGYW), beingmeaningfully included in discussions and decisions. Gender norms can be changed, and notonly AGYW but also boys and men, and sexually and gender diverse groups, can be positivecontributors to that process of change. Together we can achieve change with regards to harmfulpractices, sexual and gender based violence (SGBV) as well as unintended pregnancies.
Incoming commitment with Sonke Gender Justice

comment.narrative: CSOs have notably contributed to the general awareness of child and youth rights. Some of the activities include teaching youth and political leaders and influencing the enacting of community bylaws on these rights. The community members of Kalangala and Bukwo districts wished for more emphasis being put on education-related accountability mechanisms and overall participants stressed weak law enforcement by the authorities, such as the police and the child protection agency, related to the PtY core issues.

title.narrative: State actors improve policymaking and implementation on key issues (Improving policies and policy implementation)

# of laws blocked adopted maintained improved including the number of detrimental policies which are prevented or blocked from adoption or development to decrease barriers to SRHR and prevent harmful practices and SGBV

comment.narrative: 5 Policies/ by-laws in the districts (Mbale. Busia & Isingiro) are in final stages of enactment as a policy in their district. In Busia 1 Ordinance on Disco Matanga ( Family and child protection Ordinance), in Mbale Bufumbo S/C review of Child protection By-Law, and in Isingire 3 by-Laws on regulating the time for opening and closing bars, lodges and pool tables, Marijunana and Mairungi by-Law, and Gambling/Betting by law. The district council processing are done waiting from the office of Solicitor general for final approval. In addition, PtY started the process of re-tabling the EAC FGM Prohibition Bill and had strategic engagements with the Council of Ministers, EALA Members of parliament, and the EAC technical team to popularize the EAC Bill and seek their support in re-tabling the Bill. The key stakeholders committed to supporting the bill once it's presented at EALA Parliament. PtY will continue supporting the processes and advocate for the re-tabling and passing of the EAC FGM Bill. Furthermore, PTY supported the processes of having the sexual offenses bill re-tabled,and on 14th /10/2024 the Sexual Offenses Bill 2022 was re-tabled on the floor of Ugandan parliament. the processes of it's enactment as a National policy is still ongoing and PTY will continue to advocate for this bill to be passed.

title.narrative: CSOs amplify young peoples voices to claim protect and expand civic space
# of women led CSOs with increased L&A capacities and or research capacities

comment.narrative: The yearly target was achieved and on track to achieve the five year target. This was attributed to the digital storytelling capacity building training for CSOs and CBOs which gave young people a platform to tell their stories and sparked off online conversations with duty bearers and policy makers on key SRHR issues affecting the young people. Additionally, individual organisations were followed up to assess their understanding of the lobby and advocacy concept, knowledge utilisation/ institutionalisation process, challenges and possible recommendations. The disasgregation is as follows # of women led CSOs with increased L&A capacities and or research capacities 8; # of youth led CSOs with increased L&A capacities and or research capacities 18; # of CSOs (not youth or women led) with increased L&A capacities and or research capacities 12; and # of CSOs which are both women and youth led with increased L&A capacities and or research capacities 3

title.narrative: State actors improve policymaking and implementation on key issues (Improving policies and policy implementation)

# of laws blocked adopted maintained improved including the number of detrimental policies which are prevented or blocked from adoption or development to decrease barriers to SRHR and prevent harmful practices and SGBV

comment.narrative: PtY Uganda supported the passing of the National strategy on ending teenage pregnancies and child marriage through sensitisation of policy makers and government leaders at national level on improving the initiation and tabling of Bills and policies and implementation of existing or new laws and policies. In addition, the team supported Bufumbo Sub-county to improve their already existing bylaw on child protection to include key issues addressed by PTY. comment.narrative: The 5-year of 65 was achieved however some dropped off after the enactment of the anti-homosexuality bill. More CSOs have been identified and included in PtY activities. Tier 2 CSOs were contracted and their capacity and systems improved through training on Finance, Governance, safeguarding and Monitoring & evaluation. More CSOs were involved in PtY events such as PtY festival, policy and inter university dialogues meeting, Vice Versa festival among others. 94 CSOs were engaged in 2023 and of these 71 amount are unique engagements. Disaggregation is as follows: # of women led CSOs participating in Power to You(th) 15; # of youth led CSOs participating in Power to You(th) 16; # of CSOs (not youth or women led) participating in Power to You(th) 30 and # of CSOs which are both women and youth led participating in Power to You(th) 10

description.narrative: disaggregated in age brackets and by gender identity for m or x

comment.narrative: Several young people have participated in decision making processes and perceived their participation as meaningful. The yearly target was achieved by over 114% and on track to achieve the 5 year target. The reach was 147 females and 121 males. The reason for the overachievement was due to change in strategy of implementation. Instead of one organisation take the lead, all three orgainsations have be incorporated MIYP across all the activities done. Additionally all three organizations underwent a MIYP training, giving a new appreciation for the value of youth, which led to the change in strategy. However, the target of 60% female aged 15-25 years was under-achieved. PtY Uganda plans to have targeted engagements on direct beneficiaries to improve this indicator. Several policy engagements with young people were done and these included; -review the findings of the National Youth Policy 2016 -The presentation of the 2006 E.A community prohibition of FGM -dialogue sessions with duty bearers and policy makers -THE NATIONAL GIRLS SUMIT under the Girls not Brides -the #SMPreYouthConfUG23 brought together over 300 young people from across Uganda
